item.title: Motorists warned of dangerous conditions along Co. Cavan road
item.description: Motorists are warned of dangerous conditions on a local road. There are reports of hazardous icy stretches along the N3 between Cavan and Virginia. Gardaí have been informed and drivers are advised to slow down and to exercise extreme caution this morning. Advertisement

item.title: Man in his 40s dies in house fire in Co. Antrim
item.description: A man in his 40s has died in a house fire in County Antrim. The body was found in a house on Waring Street in Ballymena yesterday morning. The Police Service of Northern Ireland says the death's not being treated as suspicious. Advertisement

item.title: Jason McArdle Tournament to throw in this lunchtime
item.description: The annual Jason McArdle Tournament is taking place in the Peacelink in Clones today. The tournament is played in memory of Jason McArdle, who died tragically in an accident in America in 2002. Jason was a member of Clones GAA, and the club hosts the annual memorial competition each year on December 27th in his memory. item.title: Local councillor reminds people to check in on most vulnerable
item.description: Christmas is a wonderful time of year, but it's not wonderful for everyone. That's according to Cllr Brendan Fay who is appealing for people to look out for those who are lonely this Christmas. Cllr Fay says loneliness and depression is prevalent during this time of year, particularly for those living in rural areas. item.title: Monaghan GP issues advice as out-of-hours services reach high demand
item.description: A Monaghan GP has issued advice as out of hours GP services are increasingly in demand over the festive period. Dr. Illona Duffy said that the services already saw a surge in mid-December, with flu cases expected to peak this week, which is impacting both out of hours and A&E services. Speaking to Northern Sound Dr. Duffy advised to use undertheweather.ie which has advice for dealing with minor illnesses. item.title: Cavan Eagles set for Meteors showdown
item.description: UCC Glanmire head coach Mark Scannel says his team “will have to play much better” if they’re to get a result in the Cork derby at Gurranabraher Credit Union Brunell on Sunday. UCC Glanmire edged McEvoy’s Cavan Eagles 94-85 last time out and after starting the season 2-3. They’ve won their last four on the bounce. With both sides intensely locked at 6-3 for the season, Brunell’s winning streak was halted by a 73-67 defeat to Utility Trust St. Paul’s Killarney last weekend. Advertisement Trinity
